Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Computing & programming · Work & responsibility

network noun

of computers

also computer network, Wi-Fi network, wireless network, wifi, Wi-Fi, wi-fi

our formation

Traupman 261, 334: interrēte, the internet

rēte, rētis n.

noun, third declension

a network (of computers)

The classical net (Lewis & Short), used of a network as Traupman’s interrēte builds on it. Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini have no word for a computer network.

Other words

  • Wi-Fi — a wireless network

    name, indeclinable · also used · our formation

    The international name, which Latin speakers keep as a name, as other languages do; no reference work has a Latin word for it (Morgan–Owens has the heading wifi with no entry). In the house rēte says it: Estne hīc rēte?

See also computer, telephone.

SourcesLewis & Short: rete

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 261, 334, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).

Searched in Morgan–Owens (network, wireless network) and Levi–Bini (rete).

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. wireless network, wifi (no entry).
